_comment: The closed enum of suite commands the trusted measure job may invoke. This file is authority: it lives
beside the workflow, on protected main, and is checked out by SHA. The candidate never contributes a
command - not through a dispatch input, not through its package.json, not through a file in its own tree.
A dispatch may only pick a KEY from this table; the command text is whatever this file says it is.
_timeout_comment: WHY EVERY COMMAND CARRIES --test-timeout, WHAT IT CAN AND CANNOT BOUND, AND WHERE 1800000 COMES FROM.
WHAT IT BUYS. Without it a single hung test consumes the whole job: the job ends as a CANCELLATION, which
carries no diagnostic naming what hung, which leaves no capture to look at, and which the emitter can only
refuse downstream as `measure_job.conclusion` without ever being able to say why. A review reproduced
exactly that hang on this repository's own coordinator suite under an unusual TMPDIR. The job bound is the
outer limit and it stays; this is the inner one, and what it buys is that a hang becomes a NAMED cancelled
point inside a complete capture, with every other file of the suite still measured.
AND IT IS A PER-FILE BOUND, NOT A PER-TEST ONE. `--test-timeout` in node 22 bounds EVERY test, and a test
FILE is itself a test whose duration is the whole file's run, so one number does both jobs. Measured
directly rather than reasoned about: `node --test --test-reporter=tap --test-timeout=1000 slow.mjs
fast.mjs`, where slow.mjs declares three 600ms tests, reports `not ok 2 - slow.mjs` with
`failureType: 'testTimeoutFailure'`, `# cancelled 1`, and two of the three tests inside it never reported.
The file-level point is the only one the flag can usefully bound, because the file is always the longest
test in the file.
NO SINGLE PER-TEST VALUE IS SAFE, AND THAT IS A MEASUREMENT, NOT AN OPINION. Two previous values were
chosen from a run and both were wrong in the same way. 120000 came from the slowest single test point
(32.4s) and killed two whole files at 120s: 3538 tests reported instead of 3667, 2 cancelled, 129 never
run. 600000 came from the slowest FILE measured standalone on an idle 12-core workstation (273s) and a
cold review then ran the shipped command on a CONTENDED one and lost three whole files - production-
lifecycle, suite-runner-spec and two-fixture-progression - about 150 tests, at the same 600000.
So the per-file wall clock was measured directly, file by file, at the concurrency `node --test` itself
uses (12 workers on this machine) and under real contention:
production-lifecycle.test.mjs    1446.8s   (273s standalone, idle)
two-fixture-progression.test.mjs 1165.5s
shu71-trust.test.mjs              346.5s
shu241-mutations.test.mjs         314.5s
... 118 more files, all under 306s; whole run 1451s wall, 122 files
The same file, the same bytes, on the same machine: 273s idle and 1447s contended, a spread of 5.3x that
nothing in this repository controls. A value that survives that is 1800000; a value that is a useful bound
on a HUNG TEST is seconds. One number cannot be both, so this one is not pretending to be: it is the
per-FILE bound and nothing else, and what bounds a hung test is the job's own timeout-minutes.
1800000 ms = 30 minutes: 1.24x the worst per-file wall clock measured (1446.8s) and 6.6x the same file
measured idle. The measure job is bounded at 45 minutes so that this bound is the one that fires - an
inner bound above the outer one bounds nothing, and the outer one firing is the cancellation-with-no-
capture this flag exists to prevent.
AND THE VALUE IS NO LONGER WHAT MAKES THE RECEIPT SAFE. That is the part the two wrong values exposed: a
cancelled FILE is not a red suite, it is a SHORTER suite - the tests inside it are simply absent from the
stream, the plan agrees with what was reported, the summary adds up, and a claim that does not name those
tests could still reach a qualified success over a run that lost 150 of them. The emitter now refuses
success outright for any capture reporting a cancelled point, and says how many, and the gate re-reads it.
So if this number is ever wrong again the run is a failure that names the cancellation, not a green
receipt that is quietly short.
THE DIRECTION THE ERROR RUNS, stated because this flag can turn a green suite red: a test - or a file -
that legitimately needs more than 1800s now fails, and a failing point that a term names means that term
establishes nothing. That is the safe direction for an authority whose only job is to refuse what it
cannot vouch for. Re-derive the number from a measured run if a runner key is ever added, or if this suite
grows a slower file - and never raise it to accommodate a hang.
WHAT IT DOES NOT BUY: node offers no bound on a test that is not also a bound on the file containing it,
so tightening this further means splitting the suite across runner keys, not lowering this number.
